- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or -0.33), model underperforms; apply upward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for first 3–5 days if sentiment is trending.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive underperformance), model exhibits mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67), model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast by 2–4% for next 2–4 periods.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
